title: CREST CCT Multichoice Preparation
description: This module is specifically engineered for candidates preparing for the CREST Certified Tester (CCT) examination. It validates the professional and legal competencies required for high-stakes penetration testing across Infrastructure and Application domains. This simulation covers the full engagement lifecycle, complex scoping constraints, jurisdictional legal frameworks (including UK Computer Misuse Act and GDPR), and the rigorous professional reporting standards expected by CREST-accredited member companies.

questions.question: At which stage of the penetration testing lifecycle should the delivery of the final report and subsequent consultancy work be formally defined?

options.A: During the post-exploitation phase
options.B: Initial client contact and pre-engagement
options.C: Only after high-risk vulnerabilities are found
options.D: During the cleanup phase

questions.explanation: The structure of the test, including reporting and consultancy follow-ups, must be defined during the initial contract and scoping phase.

questions.question: Which methodology is specifically recognized for web application penetration testing?

options.A: IEEE 802.11
options.B: OWASP (Open Web Application Security Project)
options.C: The Richter Scale
options.D: ISO 9001

questions.explanation: OWASP provides the industry-standard methodology for identifying and mitigating web-based vulnerabilities.

questions.question: An 'Intelligence-Led' test (Red Teaming) differs from a standard penetration test primarily because:

options.B: It simulates specific threat actors and focuses on detection/response capabilities
options.C: It only tests printers
options.D: It is done during the day instead of at night

questions.explanation: Intelligence-led testing uses TTPs (Tactics, Techniques, and Procedures) of real-world adversaries to test an organization's holistic defense.

questions.question: What is the 'benefit' a penetration test brings to a client, which the tester must be able to explain?

options.B: It provides a 'point-in-time' assessment of security posture and prioritizes remediation
options.C: It replaces the need for an antivirus
options.D: It makes the website load faster

questions.explanation: The primary benefit is identifying weaknesses and providing a roadmap for risk reduction.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a 'White-Box' penetration test?

options.B: The tester is provided with full technical details, including source code and diagrams
options.C: The test is only performed on printers and whiteboards
options.D: The test is conducted without the client's knowledge

questions.explanation: White-box testing provides the analyst with complete transparency of the target environment to maximize coverage.

questions.question: During engagement lifecycle, which action is the MOST appropriate before commencing intrusive testing?

options.A: Obtain explicit authorisation and confirm scope boundaries
options.B: Disable security tooling to prevent detection
options.C: Run exploitation attempts to validate access quickly
options.D: Contact third parties to request credentials

questions.explanation: Intrusive testing should only begin after written authorisation and scope confirmation.

questions.question: Which outcome is the most likely consequence of inadequate controls in engagement lifecycle?

options.A: Guaranteed exploitation of all targets
options.B: Elimination of the need for reporting
options.C: Unintended impact to production systems or breach of agreed scope
options.D: Automatic legal indemnity for the tester

questions.explanation: Weak controls commonly lead to scope creep, service disruption, or contractual/legal issues.

questions.question: What is the BEST approach to handling evidence gathered during engagement lifecycle?

options.B: Store all artefacts unencrypted to speed up sharing
options.C: Keep evidence indefinitely regardless of client policy
options.D: Collect the minimum necessary, protect it, and maintain integrity/traceability

questions.explanation: Evidence should be minimised, protected, and handled according to policy and chain-of-custody expectations.
